Pre-scan shared supplier hash table; mark ~4K Saudi Arabia suppkeys in a bitset indexed by s_suppkey. Bitset fits in 12KB — stays in L1 cache for billions of probes.

operators.description: Single-pass over lineitem sorted by l_orderkey. Buffer all rows per orderkey group (avg ~4 rows). For each group, evaluate all conditions together.

sub_operations.description: For each orderkey group, collect (l_suppkey, is_late) tuples where is_late = (l_receiptdate > l_commitdate). Typical buffer size: 1-7 rows.

sub_operations.notes: Check once per group. Skip entire group if order is not status F.

sub_operations.description: For each l1 in group WHERE is_late=true:

checks.notes: ~4K out of 100K suppkeys are Saudi Arabian

checks.predicate: EXISTS row in group with l_suppkey != l1.l_suppkey
checks.notes: Scan the small group buffer (~4 rows) for any different suppkey

checks.predicate: NOT EXISTS row in group with l_suppkey != l1.l_suppkey AND is_late=true
checks.notes: Scan group buffer for any OTHER suppkey that is also late. Must find none.

sub_operations.notes: Only ~50-100K rows survive all filters; each probe hits L3-resident hash

parallelism.notes: Partition lineitem stream into morsel ranges by orderkey. Each thread buffers its own orderkey groups and aggregates into thread-local hash maps. Final merge of 16 small hash maps (4K entries each) is trivial. 16 threads suffice — bottleneck is sequential HDD read, not CPU. Orderkey-range partitioning ensures each orderkey group is processed by exactly one thread (no cross-thread coordination needed).

data_structures.group_buffer: thread_local small_vector<{int32_t suppkey, bool is_late}, 8> — stack allocated per group

notes: Exploits lineitem sorted-by-orderkey to avoid materializing auxiliary hash maps for EXISTS/NOT EXISTS. Each orderkey group (~4 rows avg) is buffered on the stack and processed in-place. The three subquery checks (supplier filter, EXISTS, NOT EXISTS) are evaluated as in-group scans over the tiny buffer — O(group_size²) but group_size≈4 so this is faster than any hash-based approach. Orders probe and supplier bitset check are done early to skip non-qualifying groups/rows before the semi/anti-join logic.
